inputs.root_cause: Continuing the fresh systematic pass over the 4 remaining formats' own unresolved obligations after Event 316's nrrd win. Surveyed ora's own 8 remaining obligations: ORA-MASK-001 was already correctly resolved as genuinely unbuildable (a prior tick found 'mask' appears zero times across all 3 pinned OpenRaster spec sources). ORA-PRESERVE-001's own missing_behavior framed 'was this value written explicitly, or just defaulted' as needing 'nullable defaults threaded through OraNode/OraStack/OraLayer and every consumer of them -- real, larger-scoped work.' Investigated the actual model/stack.py and codec/stack_xml.py directly rather than trusting that framing.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Added a PARALLEL explicit_attributes: frozenset[str] field to OraNode (not a type change to any existing field) plus a was_explicit(name) query method. Populated once at the single existing choke point (_common() in stack_xml.py, already called for every layer/text/stack construction) that already computes every default-having attribute's value. Verified end-to-end with a standalone repro before any test was written, and confirmed zero impact on every existing consumer by running the full pre-existing 337-test ora suite unchanged.
inputs.regression_tier: full ora package suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff

execution_steps: 1. Read model/stack.py's OraNode class directly: x/y/opacity/visibility/composite_op are plain dataclass fields with Python-level defaults (0, 0, 1.0, 'visible', 'svg:src-over'); OraStack adds isolation ('auto'). No field distinguishes 'value came from the XML' vs 'value came from the dataclass default'.

2. Read the prior tick's own missing_behavior text proposing nullable defaults (float -> float | None) threaded through every field and every consumer -- assessed this as more invasive than necessary before accepting it: changing a field's own type ripples into every read site (is_isolated_group's own opacity < 1.0 comparison, is_visible's own visibility == 'visible' comparison, composite_op_details' own lookup, and any external caller), each needing new None-handling.

3. Designed a smaller alternative: add explicit_attributes: frozenset[str] = frozenset() as a NEW, PARALLEL field -- x/y/opacity/visibility/composite_op/isolation keep their exact existing types and defaults, so is_isolated_group/is_visible/composite_op_details and every external caller are completely unaffected. Added was_explicit(name: str) -> bool as the query method the obligation's own rule_text asks for.

4. Located the single choke point every default-having attribute already passes through: _common() (codec/stack_xml.py), called identically for OraLayer/OraText/OraStack construction. Added _explicit_attributes(element, extra_tracked=()) computing which of a fixed XML-name-to-field-name mapping (_TRACKED_ATTRIBUTES) the element's own .attrib actually contains -- reusing the exact same 'is this key present' check the existing opacity/visibility/composite_op parsing implicitly relies on, so tracking can never independently drift from what those already consider 'present'.

5. Handled OraStack's own isolation attribute specially (it is set outside _common(), directly in the stack() method) by adding an extra_tracked parameter to both _common() and _explicit_attributes(), passing ('isolation',) only from stack(), rather than duplicating the presence-check logic.

6. Hit and fixed 2 mypy --strict errors from an initial dict-mutation approach (frozenset(common['explicit_attributes']) on a dict typed dict[str, object] has no statically-known iterable type) by restructuring to pass extra_tracked as a parameter instead of post-hoc mutating the returned dict -- cleaner and correctly typed with zero ignores needed.

7. Verified directly with a standalone repro before writing any test: parsed a stack with one layer writing opacity='0.5' explicitly and a sibling omitting opacity entirely (defaulting to 1.0) -- was_explicit('opacity') correctly returns True/False respectively, and a stack-level isolation='isolate' attribute is correctly recorded on the stack but NOT on its own child layer.

8. Checked whether the writer side needed corresponding changes: grepped the whole ora package for any stack.xml serializer/writer module and found none -- confirmed ora's own round-trip story is byte-level LOSSLESS (original archive bytes preserved verbatim in LOSSLESS mode via lifecycle.py), not model-reconstruction-based, matching this obligation's own prior note that the archive-level round trip is unaffected and this is purely a model-level query capability.

9. Ran the full pre-existing ora suite (337 tests) BEFORE writing any new test, to confirm the new field caused zero equality/hashing/behavior regressions anywhere in the existing suite (frozen dataclasses generate __eq__ over all fields, so a naive reviewer might worry two previously-equal nodes could now compare unequal) -- 337/337 passed unchanged.

10. Added 12 tests (test_obligation_explicit_attribute_preservation.py): explicit vs omitted opacity distinguished despite identical resulting values (the core obligation proof); every tracked attribute independently recorded; a partially-written set records only what was written; no-attributes-written means an empty set; stack isolation tracked separately from child layers'; text nodes track identically to layers; a node built directly in memory (bypassing the parser) has an empty set; nested stacks track their own attributes independently.
11. Ran mypy --strict (clean), ruff (clean), the full ora suite (337 -> 349 passed), and the 6-format regression (3780 -> 3792 passed, +12, 0 failed, 4 skipped).
12. Promoted the target obligation to implemented: the obligation's own rule_text (preserve absent-vs-explicit-default distinction) is now genuinely satisfied and tested.

.venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/nrrd tests/python/ora tests/python/xliff tests/python/ipynb tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3792 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (was 3780)
